title: Bouillabaisse Marseillaise
shortDescription: Provençal seafood stew with saffron, fennel, and rouille
note: Use the freshest mix of firm white fish and shellfish you can find
introCopy: This iconic Marseille fish stew is perfumed with saffron, fennel, and orange zest. Traditionally served with crusty bread and garlicky rouille, it's a celebration of Mediterranean seafood at its finest.

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot. Sauté onion and fennel until softened, about 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, fish stock, saffron, orange zest, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then simmer 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the rouille: blend garlic, egg yolk, and cayenne. Slowly drizzle in olive oil while blending until thick mayonnaise forms. Season with salt.
Add firm white fish to the broth and simmer 5 minutes. Add monkfish and cook 3 minutes more.
Add mussels and prawns, cover, and cook until mussels open and prawns are pink, about 5 minutes. Discard any unopened mussels.
Ladle into bowls. Serve with toasted baguette slices spread with rouille.

title: Cassoulet Toulousain
shortDescription: Slow-cooked white bean stew with duck confit, pork, and sausage
note: This rich dish is even better the next day
introCopy: The pride of southwestern France, cassoulet is a hearty bean and meat casserole that develops deep flavors through slow cooking. Each region has its version; this Toulouse-style includes duck confit and Toulouse sausage.

steps.text: Drain soaked beans and place in a large pot with fresh water. Bring to a boil, then simmer 1 hour until tender but not mushy. Drain and set aside.
In a large Dutch oven, brown the duck confit legs in their own fat, about 5 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, brown pork shoulder and bacon. Add onion and cook until softened, 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, stock, bay leaves, and thyme. Add beans and nestle duck confit and sausages into the mixture. Bring to a simmer.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Sprinkle breadcrumbs over the cassoulet and transfer to oven. Bake uncovered for 2 hours, breaking the crust and stirring gently every 30 minutes.
Let rest 15 minutes before serving. The top should be golden and crispy.

title: Confit de Canard
shortDescription: Duck legs slow-cooked in their own fat until melt-in-your-mouth tender
note: The rendered duck fat can be saved and used for roasting potatoes
introCopy: This ancient preservation technique from southwestern France transforms duck legs into incredibly tender, flavorful meat. The slow cooking in fat creates a crispy skin and succulent interior.

steps.text: Rub duck legs all over with salt. Place in a dish with garlic, thyme, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Cover and refrigerate 12-24 hours.
Preheat oven to 120°C. Brush excess salt off duck legs and pat dry.
Melt duck fat in a large ovenproof pot. Arrange duck legs in a single layer and ensure they're completely submerged in fat. Add the garlic, thyme, and bay leaves.
Cover pot and transfer to oven. Cook for 2.5 hours until meat is very tender and falling off the bone.
Remove duck from fat and pat dry. Heat a large frying pan over high heat and crisp the skin, about 3 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, sauté potato slices in some of the duck fat until golden and crispy. Serve duck legs with the potatoes.

title: Choucroute Garnie
shortDescription: Alsatian braised sauerkraut with sausages, pork, and potatoes
note: Rinsing the sauerkraut reduces sourness; skip for a more traditional tang
introCopy: This hearty Alsatian specialty layers fermented cabbage with an assortment of sausages and pork, all braised in white wine and juniper berries. It's comfort food at its most Germanic-French.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 160°C. Heat duck fat in a large Dutch oven and sauté onion until softened, 8 minutes.
Add sauerkraut, wine, stock, juniper berries, and bay leaves. Stir to combine and bring to a simmer.
Nestle pork chops, sausages, and bacon into the sauerkraut. Cover and transfer to oven.
Braise for 1.5 hours, checking halfway through and adding more stock if needed.
Meanwhile, boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and keep warm.
Arrange sauerkraut on a large platter with the meats on top. Serve with boiled potatoes and mustard.

title: Tarte Flambée Alsacienne
shortDescription: Crispy Alsatian flatbread with crème fraîche, onions, and bacon
note: Also known as flammekueche; bake at the highest temperature your oven allows
introCopy: This Alsatian answer to pizza features an ultra-thin, crispy crust topped with tangy crème fraîche, sweet onions, and smoky bacon. Traditionally cooked in wood-fired ovens, it's a beloved bistro classic.

steps.text: Mix flour and salt. Add water and oil, kneading until smooth, about 8 minutes. Cover and rest for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 250°C (or as hot as possible) with a pizza stone or baking sheet inside.
Mix crème fraîche, fromage blanc, and nutmeg. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide dough into 4 pieces. Roll each piece as thin as possible on a floured surface into a rectangle.
Spread cream mixture thinly over dough, leaving a small border. Top with onions and bacon.
Transfer to preheated stone or sheet and bake 8-10 minutes until edges are crispy and golden. Repeat with remaining dough.

title: Galettes Bretonnes Complètes
shortDescription: Buckwheat crêpes with ham, Gruyère, and fried egg
note: The batter should rest for at least 2 hours, or overnight for best results
introCopy: These savory buckwheat crêpes from Brittany are the perfect vehicle for ham, cheese, and a runny egg. The earthy, nutty flavor of buckwheat pairs beautifully with the salty-rich toppings.

steps.text: Whisk together buckwheat flour, salt, water, and egg until smooth. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Heat a crêpe pan or large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Brush with butter.
Pour a small ladle of batter into the pan, swirling to coat the bottom thinly. Cook 1-2 minutes until set.
Sprinkle cheese in the center, then add 2 slices of ham. Crack an egg into the middle.
Cover and cook until egg white is set but yolk is still runny, about 3-4 minutes.
Fold the four sides of the galette toward the center, creating a square with the egg yolk visible. Slide onto a plate and repeat with remaining batter.

title: Moules Marinières
shortDescription: Mussels steamed in white wine, garlic, and parsley broth
note: Discard any mussels that don't open after cooking
introCopy: This classic French bistro dish is simplicity itself: fresh mussels steamed in white wine with shallots, garlic, and butter. Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the fragrant broth.

steps.text: Scrub mussels under cold water, removing beards. Discard any that are cracked or don't close when tapped.
Heat butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add shallots and cook until softened, 3 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Pour in wine and add bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
Add mussels, cover tightly, and cook, shaking the pot occasionally, until mussels open, 5-7 minutes.
Discard any unopened mussels. Stir in parsley and season with black pepper.
Divide mussels and broth among bowls. Serve immediately with crusty bread.

title: Steak Frites Bordelaise
shortDescription: Pan-seared steak with hand-cut fries and red wine shallot sauce
note: Let the steak rest before slicing to keep it juicy
introCopy: The quintessential French bistro meal: a perfectly cooked steak with crispy fries and a rich Bordelaise sauce made from red wine, bone marrow, and shallots.

steps.text: Peel potatoes and cut into 1cm thick fries. Soak in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly.

For the sauce: sauté shallots in a pan with a little butter until softened. Add wine and reduce by half. Add stock and bone marrow, simmer until reduced by half, about 15 minutes. Strain and keep warm.
Heat oil to 140°C. Fry potatoes for 5-6 minutes until soft but not colored. Drain and set aside.
Season steaks generously with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a heavy pan over high heat. Sear steaks 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Rest for 5 minutes.
Increase oil temperature to 180°C. Fry potatoes again until golden and crispy, 3-4 minutes. Drain and season with salt.
Whisk cold butter and thyme into the sauce. Serve steaks with frites and sauce on the side.

title: Blanquette de Veau
shortDescription: Creamy white veal stew with mushrooms and pearl onions
note: This gentle stew should never boil—keep it at a bare simmer
introCopy: One of France's most beloved comfort dishes, this delicate veal stew is enriched with cream and egg yolks, creating a silky white sauce studded with tender meat, mushrooms, and pearl onions.

steps.text: Place veal in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil, then drain and rinse the meat (this removes impurities).
Return veal to the pot with fresh water. Add studded onion, carrots, celery, and bouquet garni. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 1.5 hours until veal is very tender.
Meanwhile, sauté mushrooms in half the butter until golden. Boil pearl onions in salted water for 10 minutes. Set both aside.
Remove veal and strain the cooking liquid, reserving 750ml. Discard vegetables.
Make a roux with remaining butter and flour. Gradually whisk in the reserved cooking liquid. Simmer 10 minutes until thickened.
Whisk egg yolks and cream together. Temper with a little hot sauce, then whisk back into the pot. Add veal, mushrooms, and onions. Add lemon juice and season. Heat gently without boiling.
Serve over rice or with boiled potatoes.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
shortDescription: Caramelized onion soup with Gruyère croutons
note: Take your time caramelizing the onions—it's the key to deep flavor
pairingSuggestion: Pairs well with a glass of dry white wine or a light red.
introCopy: The iconic French onion soup topped with a bubbling layer of melted Gruyère on toasted bread. Patience in caramelizing the onions rewards you with a rich, deeply savory broth.

steps.text: Melt butter in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add onions and sugar, stirring to coat.
Cook onions, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and golden brown, about 40-45 minutes. Don't rush this step.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Sprinkle flour over onions and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in wine and scrape up any browned bits. Add stock, bay leaves, and thyme. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes. Season well.
Meanwhile, toast baguette slices in the oven until dry and crisp.
Preheat grill to high. Ladle soup into ovenproof bowls. Top each with 2 bread slices and a generous mound of cheese. Grill until cheese is bubbling and golden, about 3-4 minutes.

title: Pot-au-Feu
shortDescription: Traditional French boiled beef with winter vegetables and broth
note: Serve the broth as a first course, then the meat and vegetables
introCopy: Often called France's national dish, this humble boiled dinner transforms simple ingredients into a feast. Tender beef and vegetables are simmered for hours, producing a clear, flavorful broth and melt-in-your-mouth meat.

steps.text: Place beef and bones in a large stockpot. Cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Skim off any foam that rises.
Add onions, bouquet garni, and peppercorns. Reduce to a gentle simmer, partially cover, and cook for 2 hours.
Add leeks, carrots, celery, and turnips. Continue simmering for 1 hour until vegetables and meat are very tender.
Remove meat and vegetables to a platter, keep warm. Strain broth and season with salt.
Slice the beef and arrange on a serving platter with vegetables. Serve broth in bowls as a first course.
For the main course, serve the sliced beef and vegetables with mustard, cornichons, and coarse sea salt.

title: Crêpes Suzette
shortDescription: Delicate crêpes in orange butter sauce, flambéed with Grand Marnier
note: Have everything ready before flambéing; the alcohol flame is brief
introCopy: This theatrical dessert-turned-breakfast features tender crêpes bathed in a buttery orange sauce and flambéed tableside. The caramelized citrus notes make it a showstopper.

steps.text: For the crêpes: whisk flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, and sugar until smooth. Rest batter for 30 minutes.
Heat a crêpe pan and brush with butter. Pour in a small ladle of batter, swirling to coat. Cook 1 minute per side. Repeat to make 8 crêpes. Stack and set aside.
For the sauce: melt butter in a large frying pan. Add sugar and cook until lightly caramelized, 3 minutes.
Add orange zest, orange juice, and lemon juice. Simmer until syrupy, about 5 minutes.
Fold crêpes into quarters and arrange in the sauce, turning to coat.
Pour Grand Marnier over crêpes and carefully ignite with a long lighter. Let flames die down, then serve immediately.

title: Boeuf en Daube Provençale
shortDescription: Provençal red wine-braised beef with olives, tomatoes, and orange
note: Marinate the beef overnight for deeper flavor
introCopy: This Provençal braise is perfumed with orange zest, olives, and herbs. The long, slow cooking transforms tough beef into tender morsels in a rich, aromatic sauce.

steps.text: Combine beef and wine in a bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 4-24 hours.
Preheat oven to 150°C. Remove beef from marinade (reserve wine) and pat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven. Brown beef in batches, about 8 minutes total. Remove and set aside.
Add bacon and cook until crisp. Add onions and carrots, cook 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Return beef to pot. Add reserved wine, tomatoes, orange zest, olives, and bouquet garni. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and transfer to oven. Braise for 3 hours until beef is very tender, checking occasionally.
Remove bouquet garni and orange zest. Skim excess fat. Serve over egg noodles or soft polenta.

title: Gratin Dauphinois
shortDescription: Creamy baked potato gratin with garlic and cream
note: No cheese in the authentic version—just potatoes, cream, and garlic
introCopy: This classic from the Dauphiné region is simplicity perfected: thinly sliced potatoes baked in cream until golden and bubbling. The result is rich, silky layers with a crispy top.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 160°C. Butter a large gratin dish generously.
Peel and slice potatoes very thinly (about 3mm) using a mandoline or sharp knife.
In a large bowl, mix cream, milk, garlic, and nutmeg. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Layer potato slices in the dish, slightly overlapping. Pour cream mixture over, ensuring all potatoes are covered.
Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until potatoes are tender when pierced and the top is golden brown.
Let rest for 10 minutes before serving. The gratin will firm up slightly as it cools.

title: Brandade de Morue
shortDescription: Provençal salt cod and potato purée with garlic and olive oil
note: Salt cod must be soaked for 24-48 hours, changing water several times
introCopy: This creamy emulsion of salt cod, potatoes, olive oil, and garlic is a beloved Provençal specialty. Serve warm with crusty bread or as a dip for vegetables.

steps.text: Drain soaked salt cod. Place in a pot with fresh water and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 10 minutes. Drain and let cool slightly.
Meanwhile, boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well.
Remove skin and bones from cod. Flake the flesh into a bowl.
In a food processor, combine cod, potatoes, and garlic. Pulse to break down.
With motor running, slowly drizzle in olive oil and warm milk alternately until a smooth, creamy purée forms. Add lemon juice and season with white pepper (usually no salt needed).
Transfer to a serving dish. Drizzle with olive oil and serve warm with toasted baguette slices.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
shortDescription: Layered Provençal vegetable stew with aubergine, courgette, and tomato
note: Cooking vegetables separately before combining preserves their individual flavors
introCopy: This version of ratatouille stays true to the Niçoise method: each vegetable is cooked separately to develop its flavor, then gently combined. The result is a harmonious vegetable medley, not a mush.

steps.text: Salt aubergine chunks and let drain in a colander for 20 minutes. Rinse and pat dry.
Heat 3 tbsp oil in a large frying pan. Fry aubergine until golden, about 10 minutes. Remove and set aside. Repeat with courgettes (8 min) and peppers (10 min), using fresh oil each time.
In a large pot, heat remaining oil and sauté onions until soft, 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, thyme, and bay leaves. Cook down until tomatoes break down into a sauce, about 15 minutes.
Add all the cooked vegetables to the tomato sauce. Simmer gently for 10 minutes to marry flavors. Season well.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh basil. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Sole Meunière
shortDescription: Pan-fried Dover sole with brown butter, lemon, and parsley
note: Watch the butter carefully—it should be nutty brown, not burnt
introCopy: This timeless French preparation lets the delicate flavor of sole shine. The fish is lightly floured and pan-fried, then finished with nutty brown butter and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Pat sole fillets dry and season with salt and pepper. Dust lightly with flour, shaking off excess.
Heat half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until foaming.
Add sole fillets and cook 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Remove to warmed plates.
Wipe the pan clean. Add remaining butter and cook over medium heat until it turns a nutty brown color, about 2 minutes.
Remove from heat, add lemon juice and parsley. Pour immediately over fish.
Serve at once with lemon wedges and green vegetables.

title: Tarte Tatin
shortDescription: Upside-down caramelized apple tart with buttery pastry
note: Use firm, tart apples that hold their shape during cooking
introCopy: Born from a happy accident, this iconic French dessert features apples caramelized in butter and sugar, then baked under a blanket of pastry. It's flipped to reveal glossy, golden fruit.

ingredients.item: crème fraîche or vanilla ice cream

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C. In a 25cm ovenproof frying pan or tatin tin, melt butter over medium heat. Add sugar and cook until it begins to caramelize, about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add vanilla. Arrange apple halves tightly in the pan, cut side up, filling any gaps with apple quarters.
Return pan to heat and cook for 10-12 minutes until apples are starting to soften and caramel is deep golden.
Roll out pastry to a circle slightly larger than the pan. Drape over apples, tucking edges down inside the pan.
Transfer to oven and bake 25-30 minutes until pastry is golden and puffed.
Let cool for 5 minutes, then carefully invert onto a serving plate. Serve warm with crème fraîche or ice cream.

title: Coquilles Saint-Jacques Gratinées
shortDescription: Scallops in white wine sauce with mushrooms and Gruyère crust
note: Don't overcook the scallops—they should be just tender
introCopy: This elegant French appetizer features tender scallops in a velvety wine sauce, topped with breadcrumbs and cheese, then grilled until golden. Perfect for a special occasion.

steps.text: Melt half the butter and sauté shallots until soft, 4 minutes. Add mushrooms and cook until moisture evaporates, 6 minutes. Set aside.
In the same pan, add wine and stock. Bring to a simmer, add scallops, and poach gently for 3 minutes. Remove scallops and slice each into 2-3 rounds.
Make a roux with remaining butter and flour. Gradually whisk in the poaching liquid and cream. Simmer until thickened, 5 minutes.
Fold mushrooms and scallops into the sauce. Season well with salt, white pepper, and parsley.
Preheat grill to high. Divide mixture among 4 scallop shells or ramekins. Top with Gruyère and breadcrumbs.
Grill for 3-4 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve immediately.

title: Pâté de Campagne
shortDescription: Rustic country terrine with pork, liver, and herbs
note: Letting the pâté mature for 2-3 days in the fridge improves flavor
introCopy: This coarse-textured pâté is a French charcuterie staple. Packed with pork, liver, brandy, and spices, it's baked in a terrine and served cold with crusty bread and cornichons.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a 1.5-litre terrine mould with bacon rashers, leaving overhang.
In a large bowl, combine pork shoulder, liver, pork belly, diced bacon, onion, garlic, brandy, eggs, allspice, nutmeg, thyme, salt, and pepper. Mix thoroughly with your hands.
Pack mixture firmly into the terrine. Press bay leaves on top. Fold bacon overhang over the top. Cover tightly with foil.
Place terrine in a roasting tin and fill tin with hot water halfway up the sides. Bake for 1.5 hours until internal temperature reaches 70°C.
Remove from water bath. Place a weight on top (a small board with cans) and refrigerate for at least 24 hours, ideally 2-3 days.
Turn out, slice, and serve with baguette, cornichons, and Dijon mustard.

title: Clafoutis aux Cerises
shortDescription: Baked cherry custard from the Limousin region
note: Traditionally made with unpitted cherries for extra flavor, but pitted works too
introCopy: This rustic dessert from Limousin is a cross between a flan and a thick pancake, studded with fresh cherries. It's custardy in the center and lightly crisp at the edges.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180°C. Butter a 25cm round baking dish or cast-iron pan generously.
Arrange cherries evenly in the dish.
In a bowl, whisk eggs and sugar until pale. Add flour and whisk until smooth. Gradually whisk in milk, vanilla, and kirsch if using.
Pour batter over cherries.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until puffed and golden, with a slight wobble in the center.
Let cool slightly, then dust with icing sugar. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Poulet Basquaise
shortDescription: Basque-style chicken with peppers, tomatoes, and Espelette pepper
note: Espelette pepper is traditional; substitute with a pinch of cayenne if needed
introCopy: This vibrant dish from the Basque country combines tender chicken with sweet peppers, tomatoes, and the region's signature Espelette pepper. It's rustic, colorful, and full of flavor.

steps.text: Season chicken with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a large casserole and brown chicken all over, about 10 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onion and peppers over medium heat until softened, 10 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Add tomatoes, wine, Espelette pepper, and thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot, nestling it into the sauce. Add ham if using. Cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Remove thyme sprig.
Serve chicken and sauce over rice.

title: Far Breton
shortDescription: Breton custard flan with prunes soaked in Armagnac
note: The texture should be dense and custardy, not fluffy
introCopy: This humble Breton dessert is a thick, custardy flan studded with prunes. Simple and comforting, it's perfect with afternoon tea or as a light dessert.

steps.text: Soak prunes in Armagnac for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Butter a 25cm round or square baking dish.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale. Add flour and whisk to combine. Gradually whisk in milk, vanilla, and melted butter until smooth.
Drain prunes (reserve Armagnac) and arrange in the baking dish. Pour batter over prunes.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until set and golden brown on top. The center should still have a slight wobble.
Let cool to room temperature. Serve in slices, optionally drizzled with reserved Armagnac.

title: Navarin d'Agneau Printanier
shortDescription: Spring lamb stew with baby vegetables and fresh herbs
note: Use young spring vegetables for the most delicate flavor
introCopy: This classic French lamb stew celebrates spring with tender lamb and seasonal vegetables like baby carrots, turnips, and peas. The name navarin comes from navet (turnip), a key ingredient.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 160°C. Pat lamb dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven and brown lamb in batches, about 10 minutes total. Remove and set aside.
Sprinkle flour over the fat in the pan and stir for 1 minute. Add tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes.
Gradually add stock, stirring to prevent lumps. Return lamb to pot with bouquet garni and garlic. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and transfer to oven. Braise for 1 hour.
Add carrots, turnips, and potatoes. Return to oven for 25 minutes.
Add peas and green beans. Cook for 10 more minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Remove bouquet garni. Stir in parsley and adjust seasoning. Serve in wide bowls.

title: Aligot Aveyronnais
shortDescription: Velvety mashed potatoes with melted cheese from the Auvergne
note: The cheese should stretch when you lift a spoonful—keep stirring
introCopy: This luxurious dish from the Auvergne region transforms simple mashed potatoes into an elastic, cheese-laden wonder. The mixture should be smooth, glossy, and stretchy when properly made.

ingredients.prepNote: or young Cantal, cut into small pieces

steps.text: Peel potatoes and cut into even chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly and return to the hot pan. Mash until completely smooth.
Place pan over low heat. Stir in garlic, then gradually incorporate butter and warm milk, beating vigorously with a wooden spoon.
Add cheese in three additions, stirring constantly in the same direction until each addition melts and becomes elastic.
Stir in crème fraîche and season with salt and white pepper. The mixture should be smooth, stretchy, and pull away in long ribbons.
Serve immediately while hot and stretchy, traditionally with grilled sausages.
